name: Stripe
description: Protects against destructive Stripe CLI/API operations like deleting webhook endpoints \ and customers, or rotating API keys without coordination.

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-webhook-endpoints-delete
destructive_patterns.description: stripe webhook_endpoints delete removes a Stripe webhook endpoint, breaking notifications.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a webhook endpoint stops Stripe event notifications for that URL. Your \ application will miss payment confirmations, subscription updates, dispute alerts, \ and other critical events until the webhook is recreated.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - stripe webhook_endpoints list to verify before deletion \ - Disable the endpoint instead of deleting if temporary \ - Ensure backup webhook is configured before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-customers-delete
destructive_patterns.description: stripe customers delete permanently deletes a customer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a customer removes their payment methods, subscriptions, and billing \ history from Stripe. This can affect compliance records, break recurring billing, \ and lose valuable customer data that cannot be recovered.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Cancel subscriptions and mark customer inactive instead \ - stripe customers retrieve to verify customer data first \ - Export customer data before deletion for compliance

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-products-delete
destructive_patterns.description: stripe products delete permanently deletes a product.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a product removes it from your catalog. Associated prices remain but \ become orphaned. Existing subscriptions using this product may behave unexpectedly \ and invoice line items will lose product metadata.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Archive the product by setting active=false instead \ - stripe products retrieve to verify before deletion \ - Ensure no active subscriptions reference this product

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-prices-delete
destructive_patterns.description: stripe prices delete permanently deletes a price.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a price removes the pricing configuration. Active subscriptions using \ this price will fail to renew or behave unexpectedly. New purchases cannot use \ this price ID, breaking checkout integrations that reference it.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Archive the price by setting active=false instead \ - Create a new price rather than modifying existing one \ - Check for active subscriptions using this price first

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-coupons-delete
destructive_patterns.description: stripe coupons delete permanently deletes a coupon.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a coupon prevents new redemptions and removes the discount from future \ invoices. Customers with the coupon applied to their subscription will lose the \ discount on their next renewal.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Set coupon max_redemptions or redeem_by to expire naturally \ - stripe coupons retrieve to verify before deletion \ - Communicate discount changes to affected customers first

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-api-keys-roll
destructive_patterns.description: stripe api_keys roll rotates API keys; coordinate to avoid outages.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Rolling API keys invalidates the old key immediately. Any service using the old \ key will fail authentication until updated. In production, this can cause payment \ processing outages if not coordinated across all systems.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Deploy new key to all services before rolling \ - Use key restriction to limit blast radius \ - Test key rotation in test mode first

destructive_patterns.name: stripe-api-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Stripe API DELETE calls remove Stripe resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API DELETE calls permanently remove Stripe resources without CLI \ confirmation prompts. This bypasses safety checks and can delete customers, \ products, subscriptions, or other critical payment data.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use stripe CLI which provides confirmation prompts \ - GET the resource first to verify ID is correct \ - Test in Stripe test mode before production
